scope: Fresh validation review of hidden reader resume, URL/storage photo request sharing, rapid retries, navigation, rotation and resource cleanup
test_changes: Added test/review/photo_alias_resume_rereview_test.dart with three cases that assert the desired behavior and reproduce two remaining findings

findings.title: A resumed photo keeps its failed local result after another consumer successfully recovers the same storage photo
findings.trigger: Two maintained consumers reach terminal failure for the same storage URI. Hide one, repair the photo, and click retry eight times on the visible consumer. The visible consumer recovers; resume the hidden consumer.
findings.cause: _startIfActive returns whenever _resolved already exists. Resuming therefore does not adopt the healthy URL/decoded generation now shared by the other consumer. The retained failed future and old failure version are checked again, and _refreshUsed remains true after the earlier automatic attempt, leaving the resumed consumer terminal.

tests: a hidden consumer resumes pixels recovered by another consumer with a new URL
a hidden consumer resumes pixels recovered by another consumer with an identical URL
proof.downloads: one rejected load and one explicit successful retry load; no extra transport duplicate was needed to reproduce the missing photo
proof.resource_cleanup: Unmount/cache cleanup returns pending/live image counts and transient callbacks to zero before the failing display assertion

findings.recommendation: On route/foreground restoration, reconcile the existing candidate with a newer healthy shared URL/decoded generation. Adopt the successful result without new signing/downloading, and distinguish it from the older failed generation even if the URL string is unchanged. Keep explicit retry bounds and prevent stale failures from rejecting the newer successful result.

findings.title: Bundled photos bypass the hidden-reader loading guard through LayerBuilder
findings.trigger: Keep an actual AlbumReaderSinglePageView underneath an opaque Navigator route, update its bundled cover photo and rotate while it is hidden.
findings.cause: SnapfitImage now guards all of its own source branches, but LayerBuilder directly mounts Image.asset or an AssetImage-backed spine preview for a single bundled source. The live cover can therefore load/decode a new asset while TickerMode is false, independently of the guarded rasterizer.

proof.test: a hidden reader defers new bundled-photo loads through a data update and rotation
proof.resume: Actual reader becomes ready and photo pixels return after popping the covering route
proof.resource_cleanup: All tracked ui.Image handles are disposed after unmount/cache cleanup; pending/live image entries and transient callbacks are zero

findings.recommendation: Gate live LayerBuilder bundled-photo/spine mounting with the same route/foreground activity policy, resuming when visible. Preserve its asset fit, decode bound and print-original rendering path. The analogous local AssetEntity branch merits coverage as part of the fix.
findings.limits: This reproduction confirms one unnecessary bundled-file load/decode per hidden update, not a network download, permanent memory leak or measured device frame drop. The AssetEntity branch was read but is not claimed as a separately reproduced finding.

verified_without_new_findings: All existing 236 related cases pass, including main cover/collection/reader navigation, repeated entry rotations, page-turn cancel/reverse, photo fallback, custom rendering, editor crop and print resolution
Ordinary URL and gs/supabase initial signing/loading remain deferred while hidden or backgrounded, and resume normally
URL/storage aliases share immediate rejected downloads and successful recovery, including actual CacheManager+HttpFileService with MockClient transport
Rapid retry clicks remain coalesced; the fresh recovery fixture makes only three signing calls and one successful retry load
Tracked resource release assertions pass; no new persistent image-handle or pending/live image-cache leak was reproduced
The fresh failures identify a missing-photo state and unnecessary hidden asset work rather than a new duplicate HTTP request
limits: Review only: production fixes are not included. Signing/download fixtures and an instrumented AssetBundle use real Flutter image decoding without live services. Resource assertions do not measure whole-device memory or frame time and do not establish the absence of every native leak or frame drop.
